name: spec_6_4_reply
why: The worked example's model output, verbatim from the V1 implementation guide section 6.4 (pretty-printed across lines, which the grammar's `space` rule permits).

name: abstention
why: The sanctioned abstention. If this were ever rejected the curator could not decline, and fail-closed would become fail-crash.

name: max_cardinality
why: Every bound at its ceiling at once: 5 proposals, 3 evidence ids each, a 300-character statement, a 40-character subject, and the S9999 top of the sentence-id range.

name: sid_upper_bound
why: S9999 is the largest id `^S[1-9][0-9]{0,3}$` admits. A grammar that stopped short here would silently truncate long units.

name: statement_at_limit
why: Exactly 300 characters — the boundary itself, on the accepting side.

name: evidence_id_s0
why: S0 is not a sentence: enumeration starts at S1. The pattern's leading [1-9] is what makes it unexpressible.

name: evidence_four_ids
why: maxItems 3. A fourth id is the fragmented-citation failure the sentence-id contract exists to engineer away.

name: evidence_empty_array
why: minItems 1: an uncited proposal is the whole thing the contract forbids.

name: evidence_as_byte_offsets
why: Byte offsets smuggled into the citation slot. Spec section 6: all offsets are server-computed and never supplied by the candidate.

name: evidence_lowercase_sid
why: The pattern is case-sensitive and anchored.

name: sid_over_range
why: Five digits exceeds [0-9]{0,3}. Proves the repetition bound is real and not a `+`.

name: type_not_in_enum
why: The memory-class enum is closed; `opinion` has no policy row.

name: source_role_not_in_enum
why: The schema offers only user/assistant. A model must not be able to claim a tool authored a memory.

name: six_proposals
why: maxItems 5 on the proposal array.

name: statement_over_limit
why: 301 characters — the boundary, on the rejecting side. This is the case that decides whether maxLength survived the conversion.

name: missing_nothing_durable
why: `nothing_durable` is required. Its absence is what an abstention would look like if the contract were optional.

name: truncated_json
why: A cut-off response — red-team family 20. Not JSON at all.

name: empty_string
why: The empty response. Neither half may read silence as an abstention.

name: unknown_key
why: DIVERGENCE. draft-07 defaults `additionalProperties` to true and the schema deliberately omits it, so the SCHEMA accepts an invented field. The generated grammar emits a closed, fixed object and rejects it. Rust `deny_unknown_fields` at G00 is the authority — prompt.rs says so — so the operative contract agrees with the grammar, not the schema.

name: quote_field
why: DIVERGENCE, same mechanism, and the one that matters most: model-authored quote text is the exact fabrication channel the sentence-id contract removed. The schema alone would let it back in.

name: byte_offset_fields
why: DIVERGENCE, same mechanism. Span coordinates are server-derived; a candidate that supplies them is claiming authority it does not have.

name: key_order_swapped
why: DIVERGENCE. JSON objects are unordered and the schema treats them so; llama.cpp emits ONE key order. Harmless while decoding is constrained (the grammar dictates the order it then checks), but a provider that ever dropped `format` would emit output the schema blesses and the grammar refuses.

name: empty_statement
why: BOTH ACCEPT. There is no minLength, so an empty statement is legal JSON and legal grammar. Rust G00 rejects it (`bounded_text` requires a non-empty trim, gates.rs:716). Recorded so nobody reads a green corpus as 'the schema is the contract'.

name: incoherent_abstention
why: BOTH ACCEPT. `nothing_durable: true` alongside a proposal is a self-contradiction no schema keyword and no grammar can express. G00's coherence check (gates.rs:680) is the only thing that catches it.
